checks.claim: Optimized design, with PTC (U.S. only): low_mwh 48.21, high_mwh 78.32. Basis: Genetic-algorithm optimization over design parameters; capital cost drawn from a $2,500–4,000/kW (nominal $3,000) nth-of-a-kind distribution, itself sourced to the NEI study above. The paper reports the PTC cutting LCOE by 22–24%, so the same optimization unsubsidised lands near $63–103/MWh (derived, not published).
checks.evidence: arXiv 2506.13361 (Abdussami et al.) abstract, fetched 2026-11-26: LCOEs of $48.21/MWh to $78.32/MWh with the PTC, and the PTC reduces LCOE by 22-24%. Paper submitted 16 June 2025, v2 revised 19 December 2025. The abstract page gives no $/kW capital cost range, so the $2,500-4,000/kW input is not checked here. Note: the shipped unsubsidised band $63-103/MWh uses 24% at both ends; using the full 22-24% range gives about $62-103/MWh (48.21/0.78 to 78.32/0.76).

checks.claim: §45Y/§48E survive for new nuclear that begins construction before 2034, then phase out over three years; the emissions-based sunset trigger was replaced by these fixed dates.
checks.evidence: Codified 26 U.S.C. 45Y as fetched 2026-11-26 (Cornell LII): subsection (d)(3) sets the applicable year as calendar year 2032; (d)(2)(A) gives 100 percent for construction beginning in the first calendar year following the applicable year (2033), (d)(2)(B) 75 percent for the second year (2034), (d)(2)(C) 50 percent for the third (2035), and (d)(2)(D) 0 percent after. The codified text has no nuclear-specific deadline: the 2034 cutoff and three-year phase-down come from the general schedule that applies to all facilities, which the shipped 'kept them for nuclear' framing does not say. Secondary law-firm summary (Morgan Lewis, 24 July 2025) also gives the 2034 date.
